title: Fud Livingston's decline and death
summary: Freeman describes Livingston as a marvelous tenor and clarinet player who drank and was found dead on a stairway in New York's Skid Row.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, poor little Fud -- he had a drinking problem and when that fell off he went back to playing for awhile and went with Whiteman where he played, but Fud Livingston
was a marvelous saxophone player, tenor player and clarinet player, and he had a great love for music, especially jazz music.

Well, he died. We were playing -- let's see, what would the years have been, in the fifties, maybe '53, '54, we were playing the Metronome -- the Metropole, you remember the jazz spot where we played up on the little stage, and Fud came in one night wearing a big Halloween nose, one of those clown's noses, and came in one night, and I thought, oh, poor Fud, he's gone, and he was standing there and he was almost out of his mind with drunkenness and not long after that they found him down in Skid Row in New York, found him dead on a stairway. But what a super talent. We are not talking about Fred Livingston, but there was a guy who burned himself out. He started out at the age of 19 and was on the top of the music business and then ended up. . .
But I don't think he knew it because he was pretty much gone, I think the last ten years of his life.
